title: Microsoft 365 admin center: user requests for blocked Microsoft-built Frontier agents
summary: Hold: the impact rationale promises that nothing changes for other users, although the briefing correctly explains that unblocking an agent can affect users beyond the requester. The request workflow, roadmap facts and documented commands are supported; the control paths and licensing citation need minor corrections.

claims.where: rationale: impact; Why it matters; Data exposure
claims.claim: Nothing changes for users other than the request-reviewing admins and users finding a blocked Microsoft-built agent.
claims.quote: Impact rationale: 'nothing changes for other users.' Why it matters: 'expect an unblock to reach every user the other settings allow, not only the requester.'
claims.fix: Remove 'nothing changes for other users' from the impact rationale. Keep 'Low. Admins who review requests and users who find a blocked Microsoft-built agent notice it.' The body correctly warns that an organisation-wide unblock can affect other users.

claims.claim: The prose reports no separately documented admin switch for the request option, but the controls table has no row for that gap.
claims.quote: 'the Learn page does not give a separate setting that turns the request option on or off'; the table contains only request approval, agent blocking and Frontier enrolment.
claims.fix: Remove the sentence 'Approve and Reject are actions in the agent's request pane in the admin center, and the Learn page does not give a separate setting that turns the request option on or off.' In Open questions, replace the third bullet with 'Is the request option on by default? Watch Message center and the agent requests page.' No new control row is required.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a separate admin setting to turn the Microsoft-built agent request option on or off.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft built agent Request Allow user to install request default enabled disable request option user request status notification; "agent requests" "default" "Microsoft 365 admin center". Opened agent-requests and agent-settings: no separate request-option switch.

claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to assign AI Administrator or Global Administrator, but role assignment has no controls-table row.
claims.quote: 'Assign the AI Administrator or Global Administrator role to the people who will approve requests'; the controls table contains no role-assignment control.
claims.fix: Replace that checklist bullet with 'Name an owner for the Requests list.' The existing Scope and Security & identity sections already state which roles can approve requests; do not add a control row.
